MC	<p>9de7_dccb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e4ebb;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, by, ++, by"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>953e_8aa6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #375e9a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>73e7_fd81</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8a4d00;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #375e9a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mp, ++, mp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22648b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ah, ++, ah"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bf2e_0cc7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e4ebb;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>bd29_3806</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kt, ++, kt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>dde2_4cd0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #733bb4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #733bb4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953567;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #953567;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d7ce_784f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fx, ++, fx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>487e_fbac</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953567;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #953567;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>63cc_04e7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mx, ++, mx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8a4d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4e4ebb;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. MC	<p>b496_80c4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dx, ++, dx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a553_3cbe</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pw, ++, pw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ea87_7798</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e4ebb;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hj, ++, hj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>7040_b309</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4d00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ae, ++, ae"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, eh, ++, eh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2bc0_e125</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953567;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #953567;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953567;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fy, ++, fy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mp, ++, mp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cfa7_7685</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #375e9a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ej, ++, ej"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4911_102a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, be, ++, be"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>00af_f0e0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4d00;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mr, ++, mr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a7e4_e017</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #733bb4;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #733bb4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #733bb4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hp, ++, hp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>177d_7033</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #375e9a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>387e_61ce</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e4ebb;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e4ebb;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>37a2_7da9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #733bb4;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #733bb4;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6ce4_d2f3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953567;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #953567;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953567;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ap, ++, ap"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>304e_8c16</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8a4d00;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4d00;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ty, ++, ty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>071c_5119</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ny, ++, ny"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>5200_ce63</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795800;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795800;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22648b;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #22648b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22648b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5ab2_4407</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924324;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #924324;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924324;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e6822;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6822;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #733bb4;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #733bb4;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>848b_7b79</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #375e9a;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b372_1875</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676001;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #676001;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676001;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, nt, ++, nt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3741;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3741;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6b;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>47cd_1d79</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #137034;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #137034;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #137034;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #375e9a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #375e9a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, np, ++, np"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
